html:
The Patriarchate of Peć is a group of churches at Peć in western Kosovo that was the seat of the Serbian Orthodox Church, raised to a patriarchate by Stefan Dušan in 1346.

The archbishops had moved here in the 1200s from Žiča. The patriarchate lapsed after the Ottoman conquest, but in 1557 the grand vizier Mehmed Paša Sokolović, himself born a Serb, had it restored, with a relative as first patriarch. For two centuries it was the main Serbian institution under Ottoman rule, and patriarchs led the Great Migration of the Serbs in 1690. The sultan abolished it in 1766. Its frescoes date from the 1200s and 1300s, and the Serbian patriarch still bears the title of Peć.
sum: The Patriarchate of Peć is a group of churches at Peć in western Kosovo that was the seat of the Serbian Orthodox Church, raised to a patriarchate by Stefan Dušan in 1346.
